front: Q: A patient ventilated for 72 hours develops core temperature >38.3°C and purulent secretions. Diagnosis?
back: Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP) / Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia (HAP).
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): [The diagnosis should be considered in any hospitalised patient who develops purulent sputum (or endotracheal secretions)... a core temperature >38.3°C, and a leucocytosis or leucopenia.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: What guides the initial pharmacological choice of empirical antibiotics in VAP?
back: Knowledge of local microbiology patterns and antibiotic resistance (similar to CAP for early-onset cases).
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [The choice of empirical antibiotic therapy is considerably more challenging... guided by knowledge of local patterns of microbiology and antibiotic resistance.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: List the simplified criteria required for nosocomial respiratory infection surveillance.
back:
1. Respiratory symptoms.
2. Purulent sputum.
3. New infiltrate on chest radiograph.
citation: Page 366 (Book Page): [Simplified criteria for surveillance of nosocomial infections... Respiratory symptoms with at least two of the following signs appearing during hospitalization: purulent sputum, new infiltrate on chest radiograph consistent with infection.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: When managing suspected VAP, which microbiological sampling techniques are preferred over standard sputum?
back:
1. Bronchoscopy-directed protected brush specimens.
2. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL).
3. Endotracheal aspirates.
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [In patients who are mechanically ventilated, bronchoscopy-directed protected brush specimens, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) or endotracheal aspirates may be obtained.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Distinguish VAP from non-infectious mimics like ARDS or Pulmonary Embolism in ICU settings.
back: VAP requires purulent sputum, core temperature elevation (>38.3°C), and specific microbiological confirmation to differentiate from drug toxicity or embolism.
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [raising a broad differential diagnosis that includes pulmonary embolism, ARDS, pulmonary oedema, pulmonary haemorrhage and drug toxicity. Therefore, in contrast to CAP, microbiological confirmation should be sought whenever possible.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: How do disordered cough reflexes and mucociliary clearance lead to VAP?
back: They impair host pulmonary defenses, allowing colonization and aspiration of nasopharyngeal/gastric secretions.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Reduced host defences against bacteria: Reduced cough reflex... Disordered mucociliary clearance... Aspiration of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Identify the invasive medical device most commonly associated with hospital-acquired pneumonia in ICU.
back: Mechanical ventilators (leading to Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia).
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Each of these is associated with an invasive medical device or invasive procedure... Pneumonia: Ventilator-associated]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Define Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP) according to its primary clinical inclusion criterion.
back: Pneumonia that develops specifically in a patient who is undergoing mechanical ventilation.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): The term ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is used to describe pneumonia that develops in a person who is mechanically ventilated.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Which criteria must be met to classify a pulmonary infection as Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP)?
back:
1. Onset ≥48 hours after hospital admission.
2. Not incubating at the time of admission.
3. Occurs while the patient is mechanically ventilated.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) is defined as an episode of pneumonia that presents at least 48 hours after admission to hospital and was not incubating at the time of admission. The term ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is used to describe pneumonia that develops in a person who is mechanically ventilated.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: What is the formal definition of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP)?
back: Pneumonia that develops in a patient who is undergoing mechanical ventilation during their hospital stay.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): The term ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is used to describe pneumonia that develops in a person who is mechanically ventilated.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: How is VAP classified relative to Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia (HAP)?
back: VAP is a specific subset of HAP occurring in patients receiving mechanical ventilatory support.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) is dened as an episode of pneumonia that presents at least 48 hours after admission... The term ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is used to describe pneumonia that develops in a person who is mechanically ventilated.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Identify the primary mechanical entry route for bacteria in VAP.
back: Endotracheal intubation or tracheostomy, which bypasses upper airway defenses to introduce bacteria into the lower respiratory tract.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): Box 17.43: Bacteria introduced into lower respiratory tract: Endotracheal intubation/tracheostomy.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: List two diagnostic hallmarks of VAP found on clinical and radiological examination.
back:
1. Purulent endotracheal secretions or sputum
2. New or progressive infiltrate on chest radiograph
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): The diagnosis should be considered in any hospitalised patient who develops purulent sputum (or endotracheal secretions), new radiological intrates...

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: What systemic inflammatory markers are used to identify VAP?
back:
1. Core temperature >38.3C
2. Leukocytosis or leukopenia
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): core temperature >38.3C, and a leucocytosis or leucopenia.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: What is the clinical significance of VAP regarding Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) mortality?
back: VAP is the leading cause of death associated with healthcare-acquired infections.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): It is... the leading cause of HAI-associated death.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Name two proven effective strategies for the prevention of VAP.
back:
1. Limiting the duration of ventilation
2. Aseptic intubation and suctioning techniques
citation: Page 368 (Book Page): Table 2: Pneumonia: Ventilator-associated: Aseptic intubation and suctioning, Limit duration.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Which microbiological sampling methods are preferred for diagnosing VAP?
back: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), endotracheal aspirates, or bronchoscopy-directed protected brush specimens.
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): In patients who are mechanically ventilated, bronchoscopy-directed protected brush specimens, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) or endotracheal aspirates may be obtained.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: List three radiological mimics of VAP in a ventilated patient.
back:
1. Pulmonary embolism
2. ARDS
3. Pulmonary oedema
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): raising a broad differential diagnosis that includes pulmonary embolism, ARDS, pulmonary oedema, pulmonary haemorrhage and drug toxicity.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: How does aspiration contribute to the pathophysiology of HAP/VAP?
back: Inhalation of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions, often facilitated by immobility or nasogastric intubation.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): Box 17.43: Aspiration of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions: Immobility... Nasogastric intubation.

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: Define Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP) based on its clinical onset.
back: Pneumonia that develops in a person who is mechanically ventilated at least 48 hours after hospital admission.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): [The term ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is used to describe pneumonia that develops in a person who is mechanically ventilated.]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: How does endotracheal intubation primarily increase the risk of VAP?
back: It introduces bacteria directly into the lower respiratory tract and bypasses natural upper airway defenses.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Bacteria introduced into lower respiratory tract... Endotracheal intubation/tracheostomy]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: List three systemic conditions that reduce host defenses against VAP in the ICU.
back:
1. Glucocorticoid treatment
2. Diabetes mellitus
3. Malignancy
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Reduced host defences against bacteria: Reduced immune defences (e.g. glucocorticoid treatment, diabetes, malignancy)]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: Why is a reduced conscious level (e.g., GCS <8) a significant risk factor for VAP?
back: It results in a reduced cough reflex, facilitating the aspiration of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Reduced cough reflex (e.g. post-operative)... Aspiration of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions: Immobility or reduced conscious level]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: Which specific pharmacological agents used in the ICU are linked to disordered mucociliary clearance?
back: Anaesthetic agents.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Disordered mucociliary clearance (e.g. anaesthetic agents)]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients

back:
1. Infected nebulizers
2. Contaminated bronchoscopes
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Bacteria introduced into lower respiratory tract: Infected ventilators/nebulisers/bronchoscopes]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: Explain the role of nasogastric (NG) intubation in predisposing a patient to VAP.
back: It promotes the aspiration of gastric secretions into the lower respiratory tract.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Aspiration of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions: Nasogastric intubation]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: How does abdominal sepsis contribute to the development of lung abscesses or VAP?
back: Via hematogenous spread (bacteraemia) of the infection to the lungs.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Bacteraemia: Abdominal sepsis... IV cannula infection]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: Which two anatomical palsies are listed as factors predisposing to VAP/HAP?
back: Bulbar palsy and vocal cord palsy.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Bulbar or vocal cord palsy]

category: Identify the common risk factors for VAP in critically ill and mechanically ventilated patients
front: Q: Name the oral decontamination agent proven to help prevent VAP risk.
back: Chlorhexidine (2%).
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Oral antiseptic (chlorhexidine 2%) may be used to decontaminate the upper airway]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in terms of its specific clinical setting.
back: - Pneumonia that develops specifically in a person who is undergoing mechanical ventilation.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): [The term ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is used to describe pneumonia that develops in a person who is mechanically ventilated.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Explain the primary mechanism for bacterial entry into the lungs of ventilated patients.
back: - Pathogens are introduced via endotracheal intubation, tracheostomy, or infected equipment like ventilators and nebulizers.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Bacteria introduced into lower respiratory tract: Endotracheal intubation/tracheostomy; Infected ventilators/nebulisers/bronchoscopes.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Contrast the expected pathogens of early-onset VAP with those of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).
back: - Organisms in early-onset VAP (occurring within 4-5 days of admission) are typically similar to those involved in CAP.
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [The organisms implicated in early-onset HAP (occurring within 4–5 days of admission) are similar to those involved in CAP.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: A patient intubated for 72 hours shows new radiographic infiltrates and increased oxygen needs. Diagnosis?
back: - Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP).

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: What is the critical factor used to guide the initial choice of empirical antibiotics in VAP?

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Specify the core temperature threshold that suggests a diagnosis of nosocomial pneumonia or VAP.
back: - A core temperature exceeding 38.3°C.
citation: Page 560 (Book Page): [The diagnosis should be considered in any hospitalised patient who develops... a core temperature >38.3°C]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: List three specialized microbiological sampling methods used specifically for mechanically ventilated patients.
back: - Bronchoscopy-directed protected brush specimens - Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) - Endotracheal aspirates.
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [In patients who are mechanically ventilated, bronchoscopy-directed protected brush specimens, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) or endotracheal aspirates may be obtained.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: Differentiate VAP from non-infectious respiratory complications by listing three common alternative diagnoses.
back: - Pulmonary embolism - Pulmonary haemorrhage - Drug toxicity.
citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [raising a broad differential diagnosis that includes pulmonary embolism, ARDS, pulmonary oedema, pulmonary haemorrhage and drug toxicity.]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: How does nasogastric intubation physically contribute to the development of ventilator-associated pneumonia?
back: - It facilitates the aspiration of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions into the lower respiratory tract.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Aspiration of nasopharyngeal or gastric secretions: Nasogastric intubation]

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: What is the approximate mortality rate associated with hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia?
back: - Approximately 30 percent.

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
front: Q: What is the specific definition of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP)?
back: Pneumonia developing in a patient who is undergoing mechanical ventilation, typically presenting at least 48 hours after hospital admission.

citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [given the diversity of pathogens and the potential for drug resistance... microbiological confirmation should be sought whenever possible.]

citation: Page 561 (Book Page): [bronchoscopy-directed protected brush specimens, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) or endotracheal aspirates may be obtained.]

back: Oral chlorhexidine (2%).

front: Q: Which conditions must be differentiated from VAP when a patient shows new radiological infiltrates?

category: Define ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)

citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [Bacteria introduced into lower respiratory tract: Endotracheal intubation/tracheostomy]

back: Approximately 30%.
citation: Page 562 (Book Page): [the mortality from HAP is high (approximately 30%)]
