category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Which PPE is mandatory when contact with blood or biological waste is anticipated?
back:
• Standard: Gloves (mandatory for contamination risk).
• Additional: Gown, mask, and eye protection (if splashes/sprays expected).
• Hygiene: Wash hands immediately after glove removal.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): Health care workers must wear gloves for each contact which may lead to contamination, and also gown, mask and eye protection if contamination... is anticipated.

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Which physical agent is utilized for the sterilization of heat-sensitive sutures and plastic syringes?
back:
• Agent: Ionizing radiation (X-rays).
• Mechanism: Production of free radicals (hydroxyl radicals) that break covalent bonds in DNA.
• Property: High energy and penetrating power.
citation: Page 234 (Book Page): X-rays are used in medicine for sterilization of heat-sensitive items, such as sutures and surgical gloves, and plastic items, such as syringes.

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What is the primary safety rule for handling sharps according to standard clinical precautions?
back: All sharps must be handled with extreme care to prevent accidental needle-sticks and occupational pathogen exposure among healthcare staff.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "All sharps should be handled with extreme care."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: How does the improper disposal of used needles contribute to global mortality rates?
back: Unsafe injection practices cause approximately 1.3 million deaths annually, primarily through the transmission of blood-borne viruses like HIV and Hepatitis.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Each year, unsafe injections cause 1.3 million deaths, primarily as a result of transmission of hepatitis viruses and human immunodeficiency virus."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: How is contaminated patient-care equipment managed between different patient uses according to standard precautions?
back: Equipment and supplies must be either discarded, disinfected, or sterilized between uses to prevent cross-contamination and hospital-acquired infections.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Ensure that patient-care equipment, supplies and linen contaminated with infective material is either discarded, or disinfected or sterilized between each patient use."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: In an AEFI investigation, which specific disposal practice is monitored to detect vaccination errors?
back: The investigator must observe the disposal of opened vaccine vials and the management of used needles and syringes for safety violations.
citation: Page 124 (Book Page): "Observing the service in action: ...disposal of opened vials."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What alternative method ensures safety for soiled linen when standard laundering equipment is unavailable?
back: Soiled linen can be boiled to ensure decontamination, providing a safe alternative for linen management in resource-limited clinical environments.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "If no washing machine is available for linen soiled with infective material, the linen can be boiled."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Which administrative body establishes hospital policies for the safe handling and disposal of infective waste?
back: The Hospital "Control of Infection Committee" establishes policies for disinfection, waste handling, and isolation to ensure high service quality.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "There should be a hospital 'Control of Infection Committee' to formulate policies regarding... disinfection procedures, and in fact all matters relating to control of hospital acquired infection."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: How should healthcare workers manage biological excretions to interrupt the chain of infection transmission?
back: Blocking routes of transmission requires personal hygiene and the proper handling and disposal of all secretions and excretions.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "reliance is placed on ... personal hygiene and proper handling of secretions and excretions."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What is the mandated clinical response to an accidental spill of potentially infective material?
back: Spills of infective material must be cleaned up promptly to maintain environmental hygiene and reduce the risk of secondary transmission.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Clean up spills of infective material promptly."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Which specific disposal-related factors are assessed during a formal immunization service audit?
back: Auditors evaluate the storage conditions and disposal practices for both opened vaccine vials and injection hardware.
citation: Page 124 (Book Page): "Assess the service by: asking about: Vaccine storage (including open vials), distribution, and disposal."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What is the core requirement for waste management under Standard (Routine) Precautions?
back: Standard precautions require appropriate waste handling for all patients to minimize contact with blood, body fluids, and excretions.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Ensure appropriate waste handling."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: What is the most critical safe work practice when handling needles and other clinical sharps?
back: - Handle all sharps with extreme care during use and cleaning.- Ensure prompt disposal in designated containers to prevent iatrogenic transmission.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "All sharps should be handled with extreme care."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: Describe the material and closure requirements for protective gowns used during clinical patient care.
back: - Gowns should be constructed from washable material.- Must be buttoned or tied at the back to ensure a secure barrier.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "gown: should be of washable material, buttoned or tied at the back"

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: Why must iodine-containing compounds be used instead of ethanol before performing blood cultures?
back: - Ethanol is less effective against resident skin flora.- Iodine prevents contamination by pathogens such as Staphylococcus epidermidis.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): "However, because it [ethanol] is not as effective as iodine-containing compounds, the latter should be used prior to obtaining a blood culture and installing intravenous catheters."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: What immediate actions must a worker take after cleaning a spill of infective material?
back: - Promptly disinfect or discard contaminated equipment.- Wash hands immediately after removing the protective gloves.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Clean up spills of infective material promptly... Ensure that patient-care equipment... contaminated... is either discarded, or disinfected... Wash hands immediately after removing gloves."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: When is it mandatory to use alcohol-based disinfectants instead of traditional soap and water?
back: - Mandatory when hand-washing with soap and water is insufficient for decontamination.- Essential for adherence to 'Clean Care is Safer Care' guidelines.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "When hand-washing with soap and water is not sufficient, a suitable alcohol-based disinfectant must be employed."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: Which environmental cleaning methods are preferred for dust control to prevent the release of microorganisms?
back: - Suppression via wet dusting.- Utilization of vacuum cleaning instead of dry sweeping.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Suppression of dust by wet dusting and vacuum cleaning are important control measures."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: How should clinical staff decontaminate soiled linen when industrial washing machines are unavailable?
back: - The soiled linen can be decontaminated by boiling.- This practice is essential for controlling environmental sources of Hospital-Acquired Infections.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "If no washing machine is available for linen soiled with infective material, the linen can be boiled."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: Contrast the additional environmental measures required for droplet control versus standard precautions alone.
back: - Standard: Gloves and hand hygiene for all patients.- Droplet: Adds face masks, increased bed spacing, and optimized room ventilation.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Control of droplet infection : Use of face masks, proper bed spacing... and ensuring adequate lighting and ventilation."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: Identify two specific nursing techniques recommended to reduce cross-infection between patients and staff.
back: - Barrier nursing.- Task nursing.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Nursing techniques : Barrier nursing and task nursing have also been recommended to minimize cross infection."

category: Discuss the safe work practices that reduce the risk of infection transmission in healthcare settings
front: Q: Which clinical symptoms require hospital staff to be excluded from work to prevent infection transmission?
back: - Sore throat, common cold, or ear infections.- Skin diseases, diarrhoea, or dysentery.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Those who are suffering from skin diseases, sore throat, common cold, ear infection, diarrhoea or dysentery... should be kept away from work until completely cured."

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the primary clinical difference between sterilization and disinfection regarding bacterial spores?
back:
- Sterilization: Kills all microorganisms, including highly resistant bacterial spores.
- Disinfection: Reduces microbial load but typically allows bacterial spores and some resistant organisms to survive.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): Sterilization is the killing or removal of all microorganisms, including bacterial spores, which are highly resistant... Disinfection is the killing of many, but not all... some organisms and bacterial spores may survive.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Identify the three most effective aseptic measures to prevent Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections (CAUTI).
back:
1. Limit the duration of catheterization.
2. Employ aseptic technique during insertion.
3. Maintain a strictly closed drainage system.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): Table 2 Measures for prevention of infection... Urinary tract infections: Limit duration of catheter, Aseptic technique at insertion, Maintain closed drainage.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What are the core aseptic strategies for preventing Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP)?
back:
- Aseptic intubation and suctioning.
- Limiting the duration of ventilation.
- Preference for non-invasive ventilation methods.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): Table 2... Pneumonia: Ventilator-associated: Aseptic intubation and suctioning, Limit duration, Non-invasive ventilation.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: A patient has a suspected vascular catheter infection. What is the immediate management step for the device?
back: - Prompt removal of the catheter if infection is suspected or the device is no longer essential.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): Table 2... Vascular device Infections... Removal if infection suspected, Limit duration.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why are iodine-containing compounds preferred over ethanol for skin preparation before installing intravenous catheters?
back: - Iodine (Iodophors) is more effective at eradicating resident skin flora (e.g., Staphylococcus epidermidis) compared to 70% ethanol alone.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): Seventy percent ethanol is often used... However, because it is not as effective as iodine-containing compounds, the latter should be used prior to obtaining a blood culture and installing intravenous catheters.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: State the standard temperature and pressure requirements for moist heat sterilization (Autoclaving).
back:
- Temperature: 121°C.
- Pressure: 15 lb/in².
- Duration: 15–20 minutes.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): Sterilization is usually carried out by autoclaving, which consists of exposure to steam at 121°C under a pressure of 15 lb/in for 15 minutes.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: List three evidence-based aseptic practices to reduce the incidence of Surgical Site Infections (SSI).
back:
1. Preoperative patient shower and local skin preparation.
2. Optimal antibiotic prophylaxis.
3. Rigid aseptic practice within the operating room.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): Table 2... Surgical site infections: Preoperative shower and local skin preparation of patient, Optimal antibiotic prophylaxis, Aseptic practice in operating room.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: In the context of Standard Precautions, when must gowns, masks, and eye protection be used?
back: - Whenever contamination of the face or clothing is anticipated due to splashes of blood, secretions, or body fluids.
citation: Page 366 (Book Page): Health care workers must wear gloves... and also gown, mask and eye protection if contamination of clothes or the face is anticipated.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which specific antiseptic is standardly used for the 'surgical scrub' to modify hand proteins and membranes?
back: - Chlorhexidine (a chlorinated phenol).
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): Chlorhexidine is a chlorinated phenol that is widely used as a hand disinfectant prior to surgery (“surgical scrub”) and in the cleansing of wounds.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the defining diagnostic sign for a vascular catheter site infection during surveillance?
back: - Presence of inflammation, lymphangitis, or purulent discharge at the catheter insertion site.
citation: Page 365 (Book Page): Table 1 Simplified criteria for surveillance of nosocomial infections... Vascular catheter infection: Inflammation, lymphangitis or purulent discharge at the insertion site of the catheter.

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What is the primary directive for sharps management under Standard Precautions?
back: Handle all sharps with extreme care to prevent occupational injuries and ensure appropriate waste handling and disposal.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "All sharps should be handled with extreme care. ... Ensure appropriate waste handling."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What is the biological rationale for disinfecting patient urine, faeces, and sputum before disposal?
back: These excretions serve as reservoirs for microorganisms; disinfection interrupts the chain of transmission from the source to susceptible hosts.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "The articles used by the patient as well as patient's urine, faeces, sputum should be properly disinfected."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Contrast the preferred sterilization method for metal instruments versus heat-sensitive plastics like syringes.
back:
• Metal instruments: Autoclaving (Moist heat).
• Heat-sensitive plastics: Ethylene oxide gas or X-ray radiation.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): "Surgical instruments that can be damaged by moist heat are usually sterilized by exposure to ethylene oxide gas."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Following a needle-stick injury, which three specific viral pathogens require mandatory postexposure management policies?
back:
1. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
2. Hepatitis B virus (HBV).
3. Hepatitis C virus (HCV).
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Specific postexposure policies must be developed, and compliance ensured for: human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)... hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus..."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Which chemical disinfectant is indicated for hospital surfaces and waste by cross-linking enzymatic sulfhydryl groups?
back: Hypochlorite (Bleach), which acts as a powerful oxidizing agent to eliminate pathogens on inanimate objects and waste.
citation: Page 231 (Book Page): "hypochlorite (bleach, Clorox)... Chlorine is a powerful oxidizing agent that kills by cross-linking essential sulfhydryl groups in enzymes."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Define the standard physical parameters for medical waste sterilization via autoclaving.
back: Exposure to steam at 121°C at 15 lb/in² pressure for a duration of 15 to 20 minutes.
citation: Page 233 (Book Page): "steam, at a pressure of 15 lb/in², reaches a temperature of 121°C and is held at that temperature for 15 to 20 minutes."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: In immunization services, what specific assessment is required regarding the management of opened vials?
back: Aseptic handling and proper disposal protocols must be reviewed to prevent environmental contamination and transmission risk.
citation: Page 124 (Book Page): "Assess the service by asking about: ... Vaccine storage (including open vials), distribution, and disposal."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Why is filtration (0.22 μm) used for heat-sensitive intravenous solutions instead of autoclaving?
back: To remove bacterial spores and heat-resistant endotoxins, preventing dangerous pyrogenic (fever) reactions in the recipient.
citation: Page 234 (Book Page): "heat-resistant endotoxin... caused fever in recipients... filtered to make them pyrogen-free prior to autoclaving. ... pore size of 0.22 μm."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What are the public health consequences of failing to dispose of and replace syringes in resource-poor settings?
back: Transmission of HIV and hepatitis viruses, contributing to approximately 1.3 million deaths annually due to unsafe injection practices.
citation: Page 262 (Book Page): "Each year, unsafe injections cause 1.3 million deaths, primarily as a result of transmission of hepatitis viruses and human immunodeficiency virus."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Identify the role of the "no touch technique" in safe medical waste management.
back: It minimizes direct hand contact with contaminated secretions, excretions, and biological fluids during disposal procedures to reduce infection risk.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): "Use no touch technique wherever possible. ... Wear gloves when in contact with blood, body fluids, secretions, excretions..."

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What is the primary rule for handling medical sharps according to standard precautions?
back: All sharps must be handled with extreme care and use of 'no touch' techniques whenever possible.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [All sharps should be handled with extreme care.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Explain the standard procedure for managing equipment contaminated with infectious biological material.
back: Such equipment must be discarded, disinfected, or sterilized between each patient use to ensure safety.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Ensure that patient-care equipment, supplies and linen contaminated with infective material is either discarded, or disinfected or sterilized between each patient use.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: How do waste management requirements differ for medical equipment versus environment spills?
back: Equipment requires sterilization or disposal, while environmental spills must be cleaned up promptly to limit transmission.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Clean up spills of infective material promptly.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Describe the clinical impact of improper sharps disposal in resource-limited medical settings.
back: It leads to approximately 1.3 million annual deaths, primarily via transmission of Hepatitis B, C, and HIV.
citation: Page 262 (Book Page): [unsafe injections cause 1.3 million deaths, primarily as a result of transmission of hepatitis viruses and human immunodefciency virus.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What chemical step is necessary for the safe disposal of patient excretions like sputum?
back: Excretions like urine, feces, and sputum must be properly disinfected to eliminate the infection reservoir.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [patient's urine, faeces, sputum should be properly disinfected.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What is the correct protocol for handling soiled infectious linen if mechanical washing is unavailable?
back: Linen soiled with infective material should be boiled to achieve necessary decontamination.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [If no washing machine is available for linen soiled with infective material, the linen can be boiled.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: How is the 'no touch' technique applied to minimize occupational risk from sharps?
back: It conceptually limits manual handling of contaminated instruments, reducing the probability of accidental needle-stick injuries.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Use no touch technique wherever possible.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Differentiate between the sterilization methods for metal instruments and heat-sensitive waste items.
back: Metal items are typically autoclaved, while items damaged by moist heat require ethylene oxide gas exposure.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Surgical instruments that can be damaged by moist heat are usually sterilized by exposure to ethylene oxide gas]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: Outline the procedural cycle for ensuring safe medical waste handling in hospitals.
back: Identify infective material, clean spills promptly, and ensure contaminated supplies are discarded or sterilized.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Ensure appropriate waste handling.]

category: Describe the safe disposal of sharps and waste
front: Q: What specific physical parameters define the autoclaving process for medical waste sterilization?
back: Sterilization requires exposure to steam at 121°C under 15 lb/in pressure for 15 minutes.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Sterilization is usually carried out by autoclaving, which consists of exposure to steam at 121°C under a pressure of 15 lb/infor 15 minutes.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: What is the primary difference between sterilization and disinfection regarding highly resistant bacterial spores?
back: Sterilization destroys all microorganisms including spores. Disinfection kills pathogens but allows some bacterial spores to survive.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Sterilization is the killing or removal of all microorganisms, including bacterial spores... Disinfection is the killing of many, but not all, microorganisms. For adequate disinfection, pathogens must be killed, but some organisms and bacterial spores may survive.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Why is 70% ethanol more effective than 100% ethanol for skin antisepsis before venipuncture?
back: Ethanol requires water for maximal activity to effectively denature proteins and disrupt lipid-containing cell membranes.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Ethanol... requires the presence of water for maximal activity (i.e., it is far more effective at 70% than at 100%). It acts mainly by disorganizing the lipid structure in membranes, but it denatures proteins as well.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Which skin antiseptic is preferred specifically before blood culture collection or installing intravenous catheters?
back: Iodine-containing compounds (iodophors or tinctures) are preferred as they are more effective than ethanol against skin flora.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Because it is not as effective as iodine-containing compounds, the latter should be used prior to obtaining a blood culture and installing intravenous catheters.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: A patient requires long-term urinary catheterization. Which evidence-based aseptic measures prevent nosocomial infection?
back: 1. Maintain a closed drainage system. 2. Use aseptic technique during insertion. 3. Limit the duration of catheterization.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Urinary tract infections: Limit duration of catheter, Aseptic technique at insertion, Maintain closed drainage.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Which chlorinated phenol is widely utilized as a 'surgical scrub' for hand disinfection before operations?
back: Chlorhexidine is the standard agent for surgical scrubs and cleansing wounds to minimize microbial load.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Chlorhexidine is a chlorinated phenol that is widely used as a hand disinfectant prior to surgery (“surgical scrub”) and in the cleansing of wounds.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: How are heat-sensitive intravenous (IV) solutions sterilized to ensure they are pyrogen-free?
back: Filtration through nitrocellulose filters with a 0.22 μm pore size to physically trap bacteria and spores.
citation: Page 234 (Book Page): [solutions are now filtered to make them pyrogen-free prior to autoclaving. The most commonly used filter is composed of nitrocellulose and has a pore size of 0.22 μm. This size will retain all bacteria and spores.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Identify the mandatory temperature and pressure settings for effective autoclaving of surgical instruments.
back: Exposure to moist heat (steam) at 121°C under 15 lb/in² pressure for 15 to 20 minutes.
citation: Page 233 (Book Page): [autoclaving, which consists of exposure to steam at 121°C under a pressure of 15 lb/in for 15 minutes... autoclave chamber is used in which steam, at a pressure of 15 lb/in, reaches a temperature of 121°C and is held at that temperature for 15 to 20 minutes.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Which method is used to sterilize surgical instruments and plastics that are easily damaged by heat?
back: Exposure to ethylene oxide gas, which kills by alkylating essential proteins and nucleic acids.
citation: Page 231 (Book Page): [Ethylene oxide gas is used extensively in hospitals for the sterilization of heat-sensitive materials such as surgical instruments and plastics. It kills by alkylating both proteins and nucleic acids]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: What checks are performed during the 'Before Skin Incision' phase of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist?
back: 1. Team member introductions. 2. Confirmation of patient name and site. 3. Verification of antibiotic prophylaxis administration.
citation: Page 261 (Book Page): [Before skin incision (with nurse, anaesthetist and surgeon): Confirm all team members have introduced themselves by name and role. Confirm the patient’s name, procedure, and where the incision will be made. Has antibiotic prophylaxis been given within the last 60 minutes?]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: List three 'Standard Precautions' mandatory for healthcare workers to prevent infection from biological fluids.
back: 1. Prompt hand-washing. 2. Use of 'no-touch' techniques. 3. Proper PPE (gloves, gown, mask, eye protection).
citation: Page 366 (Book Page): [Standard precautions... includes limiting health care worker contact with all secretions... Wash hands promptly after contact... Use no touch technique wherever possible... Wear gloves... gown, mask and eye protection]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What are the standard parameters for effective moist heat sterilization in an autoclave?
back:
- Temperature: 121°C
- Pressure: 15 lb/in²
- Duration: 15–20 minutes.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [autoclaving, which consists of exposure to steam at 121°C under a pressure of 15 lb/in2 for 15 minutes.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: By what mechanism does 70% Ethanol act as an antiseptic on the skin?
back:
- Disorganizes lipid structures in cell membranes
- Denatures microbial proteins.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Ethanol... acts mainly by disorganizing the lipid structure in membranes, but it denatures proteins as well.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the primary clinical difference between sterilization and disinfection?
back:
- Sterilization: Kills all microorganisms, including resistant bacterial spores.
- Disinfection: Kills most pathogens; spores often survive.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Sterilization is the killing or removal of all microorganisms, including bacterial spores... Disinfection is the killing of many, but not all, microorganisms... bacterial spores may survive.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: A patient shows localized purulence at a central line site; what is the immediate safe handling intervention?
back:
- Removal of the suspected catheter
- Aseptic wound management.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Vascular device Infections... Removal if infection suspected.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why are iodophors specifically preferred over tincture of iodine for preoperative skin preparation?
back:
- They are complexes of iodine with detergents
- Significantly less irritating to the patient's skin.
citation: Page 231 (Book Page): [Iodophors are complexes of iodine with detergents that are frequently used to prepare the skin prior to surgery because they are less irritating than tincture of iodine.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which specific organism is used as a biological indicator to test autoclave effectiveness?
back: Spore-forming organisms (e.g., members of the genus Clostridium).
citation: Page 233 (Book Page): [To test the effectiveness of the autoclaving process, spore-forming organisms, such as members of the genus Clostridium, are used.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Identify two proven effective aseptic practices for handling urinary catheters.
back:
- Maintain a closed drainage system
- Use aseptic technique during insertion.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Urinary tract infections... Proven effective: Aseptic technique at insertion; Maintain closed drainage.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which antiseptic agent is the gold standard for a "surgical scrub" prior to invasive procedures?
back: Chlorhexidine (a chlorinated phenol).
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Chlorhexidine is a chlorinated phenol that is widely used as a hand disinfectant prior to surgery (“surgical scrub”)]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why is Glutaraldehyde preferred for disinfecting heat-sensitive endoscopes in hospitals?
back:
- Ten times more effective than formaldehyde
- Lower toxicity levels.
citation: Page 232 (Book Page): [Glutaraldehyde... is 10 times more effective than formaldehyde and is less toxic. In hospitals, it is used to sterilize respiratory therapy equipment, endoscopes.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: According to standard precautions, what must be done immediately after removing contaminated gloves?
back: Perform thorough hand washing promptly.
citation: Page 366 (Book Page): [Standard precautions for all patients are as follows: Wash hands immediately after removing gloves.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What are the specific temperature and pressure requirements for standard autoclave sterilization?
back: Items must be exposed to steam at 121°C under 15 lb/in² of pressure for 15 to 20 minutes to ensure the destruction of highly resistant bacterial spores.
citation: Page 233 (Book Page): [For this purpose, an autoclave chamber is used in which steam, at a pressure of 15 lb/in², reaches a temperature of 121°C and is held at that temperature for 15 to 20 minutes.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why is 70% ethanol preferred over 100% ethanol for skin antisepsis before invasive procedures?
back: Ethanol requires the presence of water for maximal antimicrobial activity to disorganize lipid membrane structures and denature proteins effectively.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Ethanol requires the presence of water for maximal activity (i.e., it is far more effective at 70% than at 100%). It acts mainly by disorganizing the lipid structure in membranes, but it denatures proteins as well.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
coreConcept: Aseptic Skin Prep for Blood Culture
front: Q: Why are iodine compounds preferred over alcohol for skin preparation before blood culture collection?
back: Iodine is more effective at preventing contamination from skin flora like Staphylococcus epidermidis, which can lead to false-positive results.
citation: Page 231 (Book Page): [Iodine is the most effective skin antiseptic used in medical practice and should be used prior to obtaining a blood culture and installing intravenous catheters because contamination with skin flora such as Staphylococcus epidermidis can be a problem.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which high-level disinfectant is specifically indicated for sterilizing heat-sensitive endoscopes and respiratory equipment?
back: Glutaraldehyde is used; it is 10 times more effective and less toxic than formaldehyde for sterilizing sensitive clinical instruments.
citation: Page 232 (Book Page): [Glutaraldehyde... is 10 times more effective than formaldehyde and is less toxic. In hospitals, it is used to sterilize respiratory therapy equipment, endoscopes, and hemodialysis equipment.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the primary chemical mechanism by which ethylene oxide gas sterilizes heat-sensitive surgical instruments?
back: It kills microorganisms and spores by alkylating essential amino and hydroxyl groups in both proteins and nucleic acids.
citation: Page 232 (Book Page): [Ethylene oxide gas is used extensively in hospitals for the sterilization of heat-sensitive materials... It kills by alkylating both proteins and nucleic acids.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Define 'antiseptics' in the context of healthcare-associated infection prevention.
back: Chemicals specifically designed to kill or inhibit microorganisms on the surface of skin and mucous membranes.
citation: Page 229 (Book Page): [Chemicals used to kill microorganisms on the surface of skin and mucous membranes are called antiseptics.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: How does the 'no-touch technique' reduce infection risk during clinical procedures?
back: It minimizes direct contact between the clinician's hands and the sterile site or equipment, preventing the transfer of pathogens.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Use no touch technique wherever possible. Wear gloves when in contact with blood, body fluids, secretions, excretions, mucous membranes and contaminated items.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: How are intravenous solutions prepared to prevent pyrogenic reactions from heat-resistant endotoxins?
back: Solutions are passed through filters with a pore size of 0.22 μm to remove bacteria, spores, and endotoxins prior to autoclaving.
citation: Page 234 (Book Page): [Therefore, solutions are now filtered to make them pyrogen-free prior to autoclaving. The most commonly used filter... has a pore size of 0.22 μm. This size will retain all bacteria and spores.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the primary clinical application of Chlorhexidine in preoperative infection prevention?
back: It is utilized as a surgical scrub for hand disinfection and for cleansing wounds prior to invasive procedures.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Chlorhexidine is a chlorinated phenol that is widely used as a hand disinfectant prior to surgery (“surgical scrub”) and in the cleansing of wounds.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the recommended management for linen soiled with infective material when a washing machine is unavailable?
back: The contaminated linen should be boiled to ensure disinfection and prevent the transmission of healthcare-associated pathogens.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [If no washing machine is available for linen soiled with infective material, the linen can be boiled.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What are the mandatory physical parameters for standard moist heat sterilization using an autoclave?
back:
• Temperature: 121°C
• Pressure: 15 lb/in²
• Time: 15–20 minutes
• Mechanism: Denaturation of microbial proteins and spores.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Sterilization is usually carried out by autoclaving, which consists of exposure to steam at 121°C under a pressure of 15 lb/in2 for 15 minutes.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why is 70% ethanol biologically more effective than 100% ethanol for skin antisepsis?
back:
• Requires water for maximal microbial activity.
• Denatures proteins and disrupts lipid membranes more efficiently.
• Absolute (100%) alcohol is less effective than the 70% dilution.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Ethanol requires the presence of water for maximal activity (i.e., it is far more effective at 70% than at 100%).]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Define the critical clinical difference between 'sterilization' and 'disinfection' regarding bacterial spores.
back:
• Sterilization: Complete removal/killing of all life forms, including resistant bacterial spores.
• Disinfection: Kills most pathogens but typically fails to eliminate bacterial spores.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Sterilization is the killing or removal of all microorganisms, including bacterial spores... Disinfection is the killing of many, but not all, microorganisms... bacterial spores may survive.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which specific handling practices are proven effective versus ineffective in preventing CAUTI?
back:
• Effective: Aseptic insertion, closed drainage maintenance, and limiting duration.
• Ineffective: Routine bladder irrigation, daily antiseptic perineal cleaning, and systemic antibiotic prophylaxis.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Urinary tract infections: Proven effective: Limit duration of catheter, Aseptic technique at insertion, Maintain closed drainage. Proven not effective: Systemic antibiotic prophylaxis, Bladder irrigation or instillation of normal saline, Daily antiseptic perineal cleaning.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why must iodine-containing compounds be used instead of ethanol for central line installations?
back:
• Iodine is more effective against skin flora like Staphylococcus epidermidis.
• Ethanol is insufficient for preventing contamination during deep invasive device placement.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [because it is not as effective as iodine-containing compounds, the latter should be used prior to obtaining a blood culture and installing intravenous catheters.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: List the simplified clinical criteria used for surveillance of a vascular catheter infection.
back:
• Inflammation at the insertion site.
• Lymphangitis.
• Purulent discharge from the site.
citation: Page 365 (Book Page): [Table 1: Vascular catheter infection: Inflammation, lymphangitis or purulent discharge at the insertion site of the catheter.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What level of asepsis is specifically required for central line insertion compared to peripheral lines?
back:
• Surgical asepsis (not just standard) for insertion.
• Use of a closed system.
• Minimizing the frequency of dressing changes.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Central lines: Surgical asepsis for insertion, Limitation of frequency of dressing change. Vascular device Infections: Closed system.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: In resource-limited settings, which common procedural error causes high transmission of blood-borne pathogens?
back:
• Reuse of syringes or needles without sterilization (prevalent in up to 70% of cases).
• Failure to use sterile water for oxygen and aerosol therapy.
citation: Page 262 (Book Page): [In some countries, the proportion of injections given with syringes or needles reused without sterilisation is as high as 70%. Each year, unsafe injections cause 1.3 million deaths...]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: How does the 'no-touch technique' function within standard aseptic precautions?
back:
• Ensures no direct contact between clinician hands and the sterile parts of invasive devices.
• Reduces pathogen transfer to mucous membranes and entry sites.
citation: Page 366 (Book Page): [Standard precautions for all patients are as follows: Use no touch technique wherever possible.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which chemical agent is preferred for sterilizing heat-sensitive endoscopes and respiratory therapy equipment?
back:
• Glutaraldehyde.
• It is 10 times more effective than formaldehyde and significantly less toxic.
citation: Page 232 (Book Page): [Glutaraldehyde, which has two reactive aldehyde groups, is 10 times more effective than formaldehyde and is less toxic. In hospitals, it is used to sterilize respiratory therapy equipment, endoscopes, and hemodialysis equipment.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What are the standard physical parameters for autoclaving surgical instruments to ensure absolute sterility?
back:
• Temperature: 121°C
• Pressure: 15 lb/in²
• Time: 15–20 minutes.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Sterilization is usually carried out by autoclaving, which consists of exposure to steam at 121°C under a pressure of 15 lb/in for 15 minutes.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which chemical gas is used for the safe handling and sterilization of heat-sensitive invasive materials like plastics?
back: • Ethylene oxide gas (acts by alkylating proteins and nucleic acids).
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Surgical instruments that can be damaged by moist heat are usually sterilized by exposure to ethylene oxide gas.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What are the two most effective aseptic maintenance strategies for preventing Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections (CAUTI)?
back:
• Limiting the duration of catheterization.
• Maintaining a strictly closed drainage system.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Urinary tract infections... Proven effective: Limit duration of catheter... Maintain closed drainage.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why must invasive central vascular lines require full 'surgical asepsis' rather than simple skin preparation during insertion?
back:
• To prevent direct introduction of skin flora into the bloodstream (septicaemia).
• Central lines involve higher risk than peripheral access, requiring maximum sterile barriers.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Vascular device Infections... Central lines: Surgical asepsis for insertion.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: In terms of infection prevention, why is preoperative shaving now considered a contraindicated practice for surgical sites?
back: • Shaving causes microscopic skin abrasions that act as sites for bacterial colonization, increasing infection risk.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Surgical site infections... Proven not effective: Preoperative shaving.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which aseptic maintenance practices are critical for preventing Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP)?
back:
• Aseptic intubation technique.
• Sterile suctioning procedures.
• Using sterile water for aerosol therapy.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Pneumonia: Ventilator-associated... Proven effective: Aseptic intubation and suctioning... Sterile water for oxygen and aerosol therapy.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the clinical rationale for filtering intravenous solutions through a 0.22 μm membrane before autoclaving?
back: • To remove heat-resistant endotoxins (pyrogens) from gram-negative bacteria that survive boiling and cause febrile reactions.
citation: Page 234 (Book Page): [heat-resistant endotoxin in the cell walls of the dead gram-negative bacteria caused fever in recipients... Therefore, solutions are now filtered to make them pyrogen-free prior to autoclaving.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Why are iodophors preferred over 70% ethanol for skin preparation before installing invasive vascular catheters?
back:
• Iodophors are more effective against persistent skin flora like S. epidermidis.
• Ethanol lacks residual activity and is less effective at deep decontamination.
citation: Page 230 (Book Page): [Seventy percent ethanol... because it is not as effective as iodine-containing compounds, the latter should be used prior to... installing intravenous catheters.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What does the 'no-touch technique' entail when managing invasive device insertion and maintenance?
back: • Avoiding direct hand contact with sterile equipment or the insertion site even while wearing gloves to minimize contamination.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Standard precautions for all patients are as follows... Use no touch technique wherever possible.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What are the defining criteria for 'sterilization' versus 'disinfection' of invasive medical equipment?
back:
• Sterilization: Complete destruction of all microbial life, including bacterial spores.
• Disinfection: Reduction of pathogenic organisms to safe levels; spores often survive.
citation: Page 228 (Book Page): [Sterilization is the killing or removal of all microorganisms, including bacterial spores... Disinfection is the killing of many, but not all, microorganisms... bacterial spores may survive.]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the primary aseptic maintenance requirement for preventing nosocomial Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs)?
back:
* Maintaining a strictly closed drainage system at all times.
* Avoiding unnecessary irrigation or disconnection of the catheter-bag junction.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Urinary tract infections: ... Maintain closed drainage; Proven not effective: Bladder irrigation or instillation of normal saline]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: How does aseptic suctioning specifically interfere with the pathophysiology of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP)?
back:
* It prevents the direct inoculation of exogenous bacteria into the lower respiratory tract.
* It maintains the sterility of the airway, reducing the volume of contaminated secretions available for micro-aspiration.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Pneumonia: ... Aseptic intubation and suctioning; Bacteria introduced into lower respiratory tract: Endotracheal intubation/tracheostomy]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Contrast the efficacy of preoperative shaving versus preoperative showering in the prevention of Surgical Site Infections (SSIs).
back:
* Preoperative shower: Proven effective in reducing skin flora.
* Preoperative shaving: Proven NOT effective; it often increases SSI risk via skin micro-abrasions.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Surgical site infections: ... Preoperative shower and local skin preparation of patient; Proven not effective: Preoperative shaving]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: A patient with a central venous line develops a sudden fever and rigors. What is the mandatory aseptic handling step?
back:
* Remove the catheter immediately if infection is suspected.
* Perform blood cultures to confirm septicaemia.
* Assess the insertion site for purulent discharge or lymphangitis.
citation: Page 366 (Book Page)-367: [Table 1: Septicaemia: Fever or rigors and at least one positive blood culture; Table 2: Vascular device infections: ... Removal if infection suspected]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Which pharmacological agent is specifically used for the high-level disinfection of heat-sensitive endoscopes?
back:
* 2% Glutaraldehyde solution.
* It is more effective (two aldehyde groups) and less toxic than formaldehyde for sterilizing invasive equipment.
citation: Page 232 (Book Page): [Glutaraldehyde, which has two reactive aldehyde groups, is 10 times more effective than formaldehyde and is less toxic. In hospitals, it is used to sterilize respiratory therapy equipment, endoscopes]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What does the WHO 2009 "Clean Care is Safer Care" mandate regarding hand decontamination for aseptic handling?
back:
* Hand-washing with soap and water is mandatory for visibly soiled hands.
* Alcohol-based disinfectants are preferred for routine decontamination when hands are not visibly soiled.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [When hand-washing with soap and water is not sufficient, a suitable alcohol-based disinfectant must be employed... WHO developed guidelines... "Clean Care is Safer Care"]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Apply the "no-touch technique" principle to the handling of sterile invasive devices during bedside procedures.
back:
* Handling sterile equipment only with sterile instruments (forceps/gloves).
* Avoiding any contact between the "critical parts" of a device and any non-sterile surface, including the healthcare worker's skin.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Standard precautions for all patients: ... Use no touch technique wherever possible]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: A ventilated patient presents with new purulent sputum and a radiographic infiltrate. Which breakdown in aseptic handling is the most likely cause?
back:
* Failure in aseptic suctioning technique.
* Use of non-sterile water in oxygen/aerosol therapy circuits.
* Prolonged duration of endotracheal intubation.
citation: Page 366 (Book Page)-367: [Table 1: Respiratory symptoms with... purulent sputum... new infiltrate; Table 2: Pneumonia: ... Aseptic intubation and suctioning; Sterile water for oxygen and aerosol therapy]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: How does the strategy of "limiting device duration" interrupt the physiological cycle of infection transmission?
back:
* It curtails the time available for microbial adherence to synthetic surfaces.
* It prevents the transition from transient bacterial colonization to the formation of permanent, antibiotic-resistant biofilms.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Measures for prevention of infection: ... Limit duration [noted as proven effective for UTI, VAP, and Vascular devices]]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: What is the mandatory aseptic requirement for fluids used in humidifiers and aerosol generators?
back:
* Use of sterile water only.
* This prevents the introduction of environmental pathogens like Legionella and Aspergillus into the lower respiratory tract.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Table 2: Pneumonia: ... Sterile water for oxygen and aerosol therapy; Prevention of Legionella and Aspergillus during renovations]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: In 'Standard Precautions', which specific manual technique is recommended when handling invasive medical equipment to prevent contamination?
back: The use of a 'no touch' technique whenever possible.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): Use no touch technique wherever possible.

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Explain why aseptic intubation is a critical handling practice for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP).
back: It prevents the direct introduction of environmental or oropharyngeal bacteria into the lower respiratory tract during the invasive procedure.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Pneumonia: Ventilator-associated] Aseptic intubation and suctioning [Proven effective] ... Page 562 (Book Page): Bacteria introduced into lower respiratory tract: Endotracheal intubation

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: Contrast the efficacy of 'aseptic technique' versus 'antimicrobial-coated catheters' in preventing hospital-acquired urinary tract infections.
back: Aseptic technique at insertion is proven effective; antimicrobial-coated catheters are proven not effective.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Urinary tract infections] Aseptic technique at insertion [Proven effective] ... Antimicrobial-coated catheter [Proven not effective]

category: Explain aseptic technique and safe handling of invasive devices, in infection prevention
front: Q: A patient requires long-term central vascular access. Which specific dressing-related handling practice is proven to minimize infection risk?
back: The frequency of dressing changes must be limited to prevent contamination of the insertion site.
citation: Page 367 (Book Page): [Central lines] Limitation of frequency of dressing change [Proven effective]
